answers.evidence: रात को कोई एक बार पुकारे... तो जवाब मत देना।
answers.note: Rule is the hook; a stranger knows the premise in 3s. Not shocking, but specific.

answers.evidence: इंसान हमेशा दो बार पुकारता है
answers.note: Framed as nani's saying. It is an invented family rule, labelled so in brief.belief_label; not claimed as a sourced regional tradition.

answers.evidence: माँ बगल में सो रही थीं
answers.note: Own bed, own mother, kitchen down the hall.
The narrator obeys the rule; the mother breaks it unknowingly. Dread shifts from self to loved one.
Consequence is implied by absence. Concrete but nothing is seen.
Beats 3->5 escalate, but beat 4 (still) is mostly one idea; middle is the weakest stretch.

answers.evidence: तो बगल में जो लेटा था...
answers.note: The thing is never seen or described. Only a light strip and a shadow.
Details that are not generic: a clock at 3:07, two feet in the light strip, counting to eleven, two cups both warm.

answers.evidence: सुबह रसोई से माँ ने पुकारा
answers.note: The dawn double call answers the hook: the real mother calls twice, so whatever came back to bed is the once-caller.
Pre-scare drop + stinger is designed and measured; synthetic foley is unheard by a human.
Ends on a one-word call then 'एक बार।' echoing the hook. Loop works only if viewers connect it.
Cliché list clean. 'मैं सो गया।' is flat by design (false relief) but risks reading as filler; see weakest_line.
3D kit gives depth and light, but the face is still a drawn face; it depends on darkness and a short look.

answers.evidence: माँ चुपचाप बगल में लेट गईं
plot_events: तभी रसोई से माँ की आवाज़ आई
माँ चुपचाप बगल में लेट गईं
सुबह रसोई से माँ ने पुकारा
answers.note: Strip every adjective and the plot survives: call, answer, walk away, light out, morning returns the call.
